Landing.hero_headline: The phytosanitary footprint, from the plot to the global strategy.
Landing.hero_punchline: Measure and compare the impact of pesticides on human health, biodiversity and water resources.
Landing.social_proof_title: Trusted by industry leaders committed to sustainable agriculture.
Landing.social_proof_context: Major food groups, cooperatives and luxury brands rely on our indicators to secure their supply chains, support their producers and demonstrate their environmental commitments.
Landing.problem_title: Pesticide Risk: You can’t manage what you can’t measure.
Landing.problem_dilemma: Agroecological transition cannot rely on intuition alone. Stricter regulations, the rise of occupational diseases in the agricultural sector, consumer demand for transparency and supply chain vulnerability require an objective, robust measure of pesticide impacts.
Landing.indicators_sub_headline: A complete suite to assess the impact of your crop protection strategies across all compartments.
Landing.indicators_section_subtitle: Rigorous assessment tools to measure the real impact of pesticides on health and the environment
Landing.indicator_ari_short_desc: Evaluates the immediate risk that a pesticide poses to applicators, workers and nearby residents, based on toxicity and short-term exposure.
Landing.indicator_cri_short_desc: Measures long-term risks for workers and residents, including carcinogenic, endocrine, neurological and systemic effects from repeated exposure.
Landing.indicator_cori_short_desc: Quantifies the risk pesticides (and their metabolites) pose to consumers through food consumption and drinking water.
Landing.indicator_bri_short_desc: Assesses a pesticide’s impact on bees, birds, earthworms, aquatic organisms and ecosystems, in both short and long term.
Landing.indicator_wari_short_desc: Synthesizes the risk of groundwater and surface water contamination, and the potential effects on consumers and aquatic life.
Landing.benefits_title: Tangible Benefits for all agricultural supply chain stakeholders, from upstream to downstream, and for water agencies.
Landing.benefit_1: Protect your health, that of your employees and your neighbours: understand the risks to adapt personal protective equipment and apply best practices.
Landing.benefit_2: Secure your sourcing: anticipate molecule withdrawals and identify risk zones across your supply chain.
Landing.benefit_3: Meet label and regulatory requirements: provide measurable proof of performance (Planet-score, CSR, Zero Residue).
Landing.benefit_4: Drive input reduction: access diagnostics and alternatives powered by our AI tools and indicators.
Landing.benefit_5: Anticipate risks to drinking water: monitor and report to preserve water resources.
Landing.cta_final_title: Ready to turn uncertainty into strategy?
Landing.cta_final_paragraph: Speak with our scientists and agronomy experts to understand how AGRITEMIS indicators can integrate into your information systems and accelerate the transition of your supply chains.
Landing.solution_headline: Our Unique Approach: Data-Driven Agroecological Transition
Landing.solution_description_1: Agritemis transforms thousands of agricultural, toxicological and environmental data points into actionable insights to secure supply chains and validate ecological commitments.
Landing.solution_description_2: We provide a reliable, evidence-based measurement of pesticide risk, offering the proof needed to meet EU regulatory requirements and strengthen consumer trust.
Landing.mission_text: Our mission is written into our bylaws: supporting agroecological transition by measuring and reducing pesticide-related risks, establishing a reliable, shared standard for the entire agri-food sector.
Landing.mission_learn_more: Learn more about our mission and governance.
Landing.value_prop_measure_desc: Map the real impact of your pesticide practices. Move from intuition to reliable data via our validated algorithms.
Landing.value_prop_compare_desc: Precise benchmarking against market standards. Identify regulatory weak points and CSR strengths.
Landing.value_prop_act_desc: Implement corrective action plans. Simulate the impact of alternative products and secure your technical pathways.

Vitiscore.hero_title_desc: The reference indicator to assess and manage the phytosanitary footprint of vineyard treatments.
Vitiscore.hero_subtitle: Serving human health, biodiversity and water.
Vitiscore.hero_context: Over 1,000 spray programmes analysed (France, England, Argentina) to compare, decide and improve.
Vitiscore.hero_cta_analyze: Request an analysis of my vineyard
Vitiscore.what_intro: VitiScore is a composite score that combines two complementary dimensions of risk related to crop protection treatments.
Vitiscore.what_abs_desc: The total amount of risk associated with all applied treatments, used to visualise the overall impact of a season.
Vitiscore.what_avg_desc: The average risk level of the products used, reflecting the quality of product choices and protection strategies.
Vitiscore.what_conclusion: This dual perspective highlights both the volume of impact and the quality of choices, guiding credible and measurable action plans. VitiScore also helps minimise climatic and regional effects and makes it easier to compare strategies across regions, climates and countries.
Vitiscore.coaching_intro: VitiScore is not just a score delivered at the end of the process. Our team works hand in hand with your vineyard teams to turn every analysis into a concrete, measurable improvement lever.
Vitiscore.coaching_step1_desc: We analyse your spray schedules and identify the most impactful molecules along with concrete substitution options tailored to your context.
Vitiscore.coaching_step2_desc: We calculate the VitiScore on your forecast schedules to measure the effect of each planned change upstream, before implementation in the vineyard.
Vitiscore.coaching_step3_desc: Season after season, we measure your progress and adjust recommendations to build a continuous, documented improvement trajectory.
Vitiscore.coaching_conclusion: This operational advisory is a decisive asset in the context of the CSRD and growing environmental traceability requirements.
Vitiscore.how_intro: VitiScore is based on AGRITEMIS scientific indicators, which assess pesticide risks on human health, consumers, biodiversity and water.
Vitiscore.indicator_ari_desc: Assesses immediate risks for applicators, workers and nearby residents during treatments.
Vitiscore.indicator_cri_desc: Measures long-term effects of repeated exposure (carcinogenic, endocrine, neurological, etc.).
Vitiscore.indicator_cori_desc: Quantifies the risk through food products and drinking water, including metabolites.
Vitiscore.indicator_bri_desc: Evaluates the impact on bees, birds, earthworms, aquatic organisms and ecosystems.
Vitiscore.indicator_wari_desc: Summarises the risk of groundwater and surface water contamination, for both fauna and consumers.
Vitiscore.analyze_item_1: Your spray programmes: products, doses, frequencies, dates, crops and blocks.
Vitiscore.analyze_item_2: Risk aggregation at plot, farm and group level when multiple estates are involved.
Vitiscore.analyze_item_3: Internal benchmarks (between estates and blocks) and external benchmarks (basins, regions, years).
Vitiscore.analyze_item_4: Identification of reduction levers: substitutions, biocontrol, dose adjustments and strategy optimisation.
Vitiscore.uses_benchmark_desc: Compare practices between estates, regions and countries to identify leaders, gaps and improvement margins.
Vitiscore.uses_strategy_desc: Track the effect of changes (before/after), set vintage targets and manage reduction trajectories.
Vitiscore.uses_kpi_desc: Integrate VitiScore into CSR, purchasing, quality or internal certification dashboards for ongoing monitoring.
Vitiscore.uses_hr_desc: Use VitiScore as an indicator for internal recognition or bonuses linked to environmental performance.
Vitiscore.audience_groups_desc: Multi-estate management, international comparisons and alignment of crop protection strategies at group level.
Vitiscore.audience_domains_desc: Continuous improvement of practices and structured dialogue between technical teams, management and owners.
Vitiscore.audience_interprof_desc: Collective benchmarks, shared reduction pathways and support schemes for members.
Vitiscore.deliverables_item_1: VitiScore at plot and farm level, plus a consolidated group synthesis.
Vitiscore.deliverables_item_2: Risk profile (ARI, CRI, CORI, BRI, WARI) with strengths and points of attention.
Vitiscore.deliverables_item_3: Visual benchmarks (maps, boxplots, radar charts, time series) to compare situations.
Vitiscore.deliverables_item_4: Action plan: alternatives, priority substitutions and reduction targets by season or vintage.
Vitiscore.data_text: More than 1,000 spray programmes have already been analysed (France, England, Argentina), providing robust references to compare your practices. The methodology can be extended to other regions, appellations and countries depending on your projects.
Vitiscore.integrations_item_1: Formats: executive PDF reports, CSV exports and API connections to your information systems, ERPs or farm management software.
Vitiscore.integrations_item_2: Interoperability: possible connection with your existing databases, traceability tools and BI dashboards.
Vitiscore.cta_text: To launch a VitiScore analysis, you upload your spray programmes (CSV/XLSX) and specify your objectives: benchmarking, internal KPIs, communication, bonus schemes, etc. AGRITEMIS provides a quote and, if needed, a sample output on a subset of plots.
Vitiscore.disclaimer_text: VitiScore is a tool developed by AGRITEMIS. It is based on AGRITEMIS indicators (ARI, CRI, CORI, BRI) and a consolidated, documented and reproducible method.

Indicators.title: Our Indicators
Indicators.subtitle: Five complementary indicators for a comprehensive assessment of pesticide risk at every stage of the agricultural chain.
Indicators.eiq_subtitle: A new generation of more precise and more relevant indicators.
Indicators.eiq_paragraph_1: The Environmental Impact Quotient (EIQ), developed in the 1990s, was a first step towards quantifying pesticide risk. However, its limitations are now well documented: no weighting by actual dose, lack of granularity by environmental compartment, and outdated toxicological data.
Indicators.eiq_paragraph_2: AGRITEMIS indicators address these shortcomings by integrating the most recent European regulatory and toxicological data, weighting each assessment by actually applied doses, and distinguishing five independent risk compartments — human health, biodiversity, water resources, soil and overall ecotoxicity.
Indicators.eiq_paragraph_3: AGRITEMIS indicators are part of a continuous improvement dynamic: we integrate new societal concerns related to pesticide risks — such as PFAS — as soon as a robust scientific basis allows these new findings to be objectively assessed.
Indicators.cta_subtitle: Receive the complete documentation of our scientific methodology.
Indicators.molecule_subtitle: AGRITEMIS indicators are assessed at three successive scales: the active substance, the phytosanitary product at its dose, and the complete crop treatment calendar.
Indicators.source_1: The physicochemical, toxicological and ecotoxicological properties of active substances (PPDB, BPDB — Pesticide and Biopesticide Property Database): half-life, mobility, lethal doses, CLP hazard statements, persistence in living tissues, etc.
Indicators.source_2: Regulatory data on phytosanitary products: CLP hazard statements, formulation, composition, reference dose.
Indicators.source_3: The actual dose of product applied.
Indicators.ari_desc: Acute toxicity risk for agricultural workers.
Indicators.cri_desc: Chronic toxicity risk for agricultural workers.
Indicators.bri_criteria: Toxicity per organism × persistence & transfer to water
Indicators.cori_desc: Risk to consumers via crop and groundwater contamination.
Indicators.wari_desc: Water pollution risk for water consumers and the aquatic environment.
Indicators.wari_note: FISH is the same sub-indicator as in BRI

Waterscore.hero_title_desc: Measure and manage the pesticide footprint on water resources.
Waterscore.hero_subtitle: From the field to group-level strategic management.
Waterscore.hero_context: An integrated bottom-up platform for full traceability of water impact, designed to meet CSRD requirements.
Waterscore.what_intro: The WaterScore is a composite score [0–100] that quantifies the water resource footprint of all phytosanitary treatments in a crop calendar. The lower the cumulative risk, the higher the WaterScore. Field conditions — slope, proximity to watercourses, catchment areas, soil type and rainfall events following applications — modulate the score to reflect good practices and climatic-geographical risks.
Waterscore.what_wari_desc: Each active substance is assessed by the WARI (Water and Aquatic Risk Index), which combines aquatic toxicity with exposure pathways: runoff, leaching and groundwater contamination.
Waterscore.what_cumul_desc: The WARI of each applied product is aggregated across the full treatment calendar, providing a comprehensive view of water pressure at field level.
Waterscore.what_score_desc: The cumulative WARI is transformed into an inverse score: the lower the risk, the higher the WaterScore. A score of 100 represents a calendar with no measurable water impact.
Waterscore.what_conclusion: The WaterScore integrates secondary metabolites, SDHIs, PFAS (forever chemicals) and distinguishes acute and chronic risks for a comprehensive assessment.
Waterscore.architecture_title: A bottom-up architecture for full traceability
Waterscore.architecture_intro: The WaterScore is part of a four-level interconnected analysis. Every aggregated indicator is traceable to its source, ensuring full transparency for ESG/CSRD reporting.
Waterscore.architecture_level1_desc: Precise geolocation, treatment calendars and WaterScore calculation at individual field level.
Waterscore.architecture_level2_desc: Temporal analysis, forecast calendars, leaching alerts and support from our agronomic AI.
Waterscore.architecture_level3_desc: Entity-level data aggregation, comparative analysis and treatment portfolio optimisation.
Waterscore.architecture_level4_desc: Group dashboards, cross-region and cross-country benchmarks, sustainability reporting and overall strategic alignment.
Waterscore.architecture_conclusion: KPIs aggregated at each scale of interest (region, country, world) are the exact and verifiable reflection of data collected at individual field level.
Waterscore.wari_intro: The WARI (Water and Aquatic Risk Index) assesses the risk of water pollution for consumers and the aquatic environment. It combines two complementary dimensions.
Waterscore.wari_toxicity_desc: Assessment of acute toxicity (LC50 96h), chronic toxicity (NOEC 21d) and H400-H413 hazard statements, for the active substance (75%) and its secondary metabolites (25%).
Waterscore.wari_exposure_desc: Analysis of transfer pathways to surface water (Koc, DT50) and groundwater (GUS), including detection of PFAS molecules whose exposure factors are set to maximum.
Waterscore.indicators_intro: The WaterScore complements the AGRITEMIS indicator suite to deliver a 360° view of pesticide risk.
Waterscore.regulatory_intro: The CSRD directive requires precise traceability of environmental impacts, particularly on water resources. The WaterScore provides the structured and verifiable data that is now essential.
Waterscore.regulatory_csrd_desc: Standardised and auditable indicators, integrated into a traceable data architecture from field to group, for robust environmental reporting.
Waterscore.regulatory_traceability_desc: Every aggregated data point is verifiable back to its field source. This transparency is a decisive advantage for growing regulator and stakeholder expectations.
Waterscore.uses_benchmark_desc: Compare WaterScore across fields, farms, regions and growing seasons to identify best practices and improvement margins.
Waterscore.uses_optimize_desc: Simulate the effect of molecule substitution on the WaterScore before the season to make informed decisions.
Waterscore.uses_report_desc: Produce verifiable KPIs on the water footprint of your agricultural activities for your ESG and CSRD reports.
Waterscore.uses_anticipate_desc: Identify at-risk substances in your programmes and prepare substitution plans ahead of regulatory restrictions.
Waterscore.audience_groups_desc: Manage the water footprint of your agricultural supply chain globally and feed your CSRD reporting with traceable data.
Waterscore.audience_water_desc: Assess and monitor pesticide pressure on watersheds, catchment areas and groundwater with scientific indicators.
Waterscore.audience_coops_desc: Support your members in reducing their water impact with precise diagnostics and measurable improvement trajectories.
Waterscore.cta_text: Talk to our experts to discover how the WaterScore can integrate with your information system and support your CSRD obligations.

Indicator_ari.card_subtitle: Acute toxicity risk for the applicator, agricultural workers, neighbours and re-entry personnel
Indicator_ari.description: The ARI combines the acute toxicity of a substance with the exposure of each population group: applicator (factor ×10), workers and neighbours (volatilisation factor) and re-entry personnel (crop persistence).
Indicator_ari.left_section_1_items: Dermal toxicity (LD50)|Inhalation toxicity (LC50)|Eye irritation (CLP + PPDB)|Skin allergies (CLP + PPDB)|Maximum value retained
Indicator_ari.left_section_2_items: Applicator: factor ×10 (direct contact)|Workers & Neighbours: volatilisation (vapour pressure, Henry's constant)|Re-entry: crop persistence (DT50 crop)|PFAS (forever pollutant): maximum exposure
Indicator_ari.right_section_1_items: Same criteria as the active substance
Indicator_ari.right_section_2_items: Same criteria as the active substance|PFAS (forever pollutant): maximum exposure
Indicator_ari.formula: Score = max among secondary metabolites referenced in PPDB / BPDB
Indicator_ari.pfas_warning: PFAS warning: any substance or metabolite identified as PFAS (forever pollutant) has its exposure factors set to maximum.
Indicator_ari.sources_desc: Toxicological data come from PPDB, BPDB and European CLP classifications. Exposure parameters (vapour pressure, Henry's constant, DT50) are from European approval dossiers.
Indicator_ari.cta_final_desc: ARI integrates into the VitiScore and WaterScore composite scores, and can be used individually to assess the acute risk of each active substance.

Indicator_cri.card_subtitle: Chronic toxicity risk for the applicator, agricultural workers and neighbours
Indicator_cri.description: The CRI combines chronic toxicity effects of a substance with environmental persistence and exposure pathways specific to each population. It distinguishes applicator exposure (factor ×10) from workers and neighbours (volatilisation factor).
Indicator_cri.left_section_2_items: Environmental persistence (soil, crop, living tissues)|Molecule volatility|PFAS (forever pollutant)
Indicator_cri.right_section_1_items: Same criteria as the active substance
Indicator_cri.right_section_2_items: Environmental persistence (soil, crop, living tissues)|PFAS (forever pollutant)
Indicator_cri.formula: Score = max among secondary metabolites referenced in PPDB / BPDB
Indicator_cri.pfas_warning: PFAS warning: any substance or metabolite identified as PFAS (forever pollutant) has its exposure factors set to maximum.
Indicator_cri.sources_desc: Chronic toxicity data come from CLP classifications (hazard statements), PPDB (Health Issues) and European approval dossiers. Persistence parameters (DT50, BCF) are from the same sources.
Indicator_cri.cta_final_desc: CRI integrates into the VitiScore composite score and helps identify substances with the highest chronic health risks.

Indicator_cori.card_subtitle: Risk to consumers from crop contamination and water contamination
Indicator_cori.description: CORI combines two contamination pathways: crop contamination (CORIcrop) and groundwater contamination (CORIwater), each combining chronic toxicity with specific exposure factors.
Indicator_cori.left_section_2_items: CORIcrop: DT50 crop, DT50 soil, systemic factor (×3 if systemic)|CORIwater: leaching (GUS), runoff (Koc, DT50 soil)|PFAS (forever pollutant): maximum exposure
Indicator_cori.right_section_1_items: Same criteria as the active substance
Indicator_cori.right_section_2_items: Same criteria as the active substance|PFAS (forever pollutant): maximum exposure
Indicator_cori.formula: Score = max among secondary metabolites referenced in PPDB / BPDB
Indicator_cori.pfas_warning: PFAS warning: any substance or metabolite identified as PFAS (forever pollutant) has its exposure factors set to maximum.
Indicator_cori.sources_desc: Chronic toxicity data and transfer parameters (GUS, Koc, DT50, systemic factor) come from PPDB, BPDB and European approval dossiers.
Indicator_cori.cta_final_desc: CORI identifies substances posing the greatest consumer risk and helps prioritise substitution plans.

Indicator_bri.card_subtitle: Risk to biodiversity: bees, birds, earthworms and fish
Indicator_bri.description: BRI assesses toxicity for four non-target organism groups. Each organism is assessed independently with a ×3 multiplier, then scores are aggregated.
Indicator_bri.left_section_1_items: Bees: contact and oral LD50 (min retained)|Birds: acute oral LD50 and chronic NOEL 21d (max retained)|Earthworms: LC50 14d and reproduction NOEC (max retained)|Fish: LC50 96h, NOEC 21d and hazard statements H400-H413 (max retained)
Indicator_bri.left_section_2_items: Bees: DT50 crop|Birds: max(DT50 crop, DT50 soil)|Earthworms: DT50 soil|Fish: leaching (GUS, DT50 soil) and runoff (Koc, DT50 soil)|PFAS: maximum exposure
Indicator_bri.right_section_1_items: Same criteria as the active substance per organism
Indicator_bri.right_section_2_items: Same criteria as the active substance per organism|PFAS (forever pollutant): maximum exposure
Indicator_bri.formula: Score = max among secondary metabolites for each organism (PPDB / BPDB)
Indicator_bri.pfas_warning: PFAS warning: any substance or metabolite identified as PFAS (forever pollutant) has its exposure factors set to maximum.
Indicator_bri.sources_desc: Ecotoxicological data (LD50, LC50, NOEC, NOEL) come from PPDB and BPDB. Environmental parameters (DT50, Koc, GUS) are from European approval dossiers and CLP classifications.
Indicator_bri.cta_final_desc: BRI integrates into VitiScore and identifies the most impactful substances for biodiversity to prioritise substitutions.

Indicator_wari.card_subtitle: Water pollution risk for the aquatic environment and water consumers
Indicator_wari.description: WARI combines two components: the risk for water consumers via groundwater contamination (CORIwater) and the aquatic toxicity risk for fish (FISH). WARI = CORIwater + FISH.
Indicator_wari.left_section_1_items: CORIwater: carcinogenicity, neurotoxicity, endocrine disruption, SDHI, mitochondrial disruption|FISH: acute toxicity (LC50 96h), chronic (NOEC 21d), hazard statements H400-H413|Maximum value retained
Indicator_wari.left_section_2_items: Runoff to surface water (Koc, DT50 soil)|Leaching to groundwater (GUS, DT50 soil)|Maximum exposure pathway retained|PFAS (forever pollutant): maximum exposure
Indicator_wari.right_section_1_items: Same criteria as the active substance
Indicator_wari.right_section_2_items: Same criteria as the active substance|PFAS (forever pollutant): maximum exposure
Indicator_wari.formula: WARI = CORIwater + FISH — Score = max among metabolites (PPDB / BPDB)
Indicator_wari.pfas_warning: PFAS warning: any substance or metabolite identified as PFAS (forever pollutant) has its exposure factors set to maximum. This is particularly critical for WARI as PFAS are persistent water pollutants.
Indicator_wari.sources_desc: Aquatic toxicity data (LC50, NOEC) and transfer parameters (GUS, Koc, DT50) come from PPDB, BPDB and European approval dossiers. CLP classifications (H400-H413) complete the assessment.
Indicator_wari.cta_final_desc: WARI is the building block of WaterScore. It identifies the most impactful substances for water resources and guides substitution plans.
